PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
REFERRING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE OF COLLECTION: [redacted date]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Twin pregnancy at 17 weeks gestation by ultrasound dating. Ultrasound abnormalities detected in Twin 2 (smaller twin, positioned higher on maternal right) including cardiac defect. Sample requested for chromosomal analysis.

SAMPLE TYPE
Amniotic fluid from Twin 2

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection
- Chromosomes analyzed: 13, 18, and 21
- Method: Multiplex PCR amplification of short tandem repeat (STR) markers
- Platform: Applied Biosystems 3500 Genetic Analyzer

RESULT
SAMPLE UNSUITABLE FOR ANALYSIS

Two distinct genotypes detected at significant levels across multiple STR markers, preventing reliable interpretation of fetal chromosome copy number. The amniotic fluid sample showed blood-stained cell pellet upon receipt, indicating maternal cell contamination.

TECHNICAL DETAILS
QF-PCR analysis revealed mixed profiles with maternal and fetal allele peaks present at ratios incompatible with standard trisomy interpretation algorithms. The presence of maternal cells at >20% prevents accurate determination of fetal chromosome status.

FOLLOW-UP TESTING
1. Cell culture has been initiated from the original amniotic fluid sample
2. Karyotype analysis will be performed on cultured amniocytes
3. Repeat QF-PCR will be attempted on cultured cells
4. Expected turnaround time: 10-14 days from culture initiation

RECOMMENDATIONS
Await results from cultured amniocyte analysis. The cultured cells should provide pure fetal material for accurate chromosomal assessment. Clinical management decisions should be deferred until definitive results are available.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
